newsitem.title: USA: No immediate plans for US food aid to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: No immediate plans for US food aid to N.Korea.

text.p: The U.S. government has no immediate plans to give food aid to famine-struck North Korea, but is watching the situation there closely, said a State Department official on Thursday.

"While the U.S. government has no immediate plans to provide food assistance to North Korea, we are continuing to monitor the situation there closely," said Charles Kartman, acting assistant secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific affairs.
He said the U.S. government will likely decide in the next few weeks on what its next move will be.

"I think that over the next few weeks we will try to come up with the decisions on what to do next," Kartman told a press briefing after a conference between officials from non-governmental organizations and State Department on Korea.
Aid organizations urged the United States to quickly provide more help to North Korea and said the country is experiencing a life-threatening food shortage that could soon take on famine proportions.
Don Krumm of Refugees International said severe malnutrition could begin in Korea by May, but the harvest will not begin until September, leaving "five very vulnerable months."
Krumm said the situation for North Korea's 23 million people is "urgent and critical," and called upon the U.S. government to "exert the global leadership to avert disaster."
Krumm said that so far the U.S. provided "token food aid" and called Washington's response to Korea "lethargic."

Kartman, while denying the U.S. response was lethargic, said a U.S. analysis of Korea is "substantially in agreement" with that of the aid organizations. State Department will now study the information and come up with the appropriate response, Kartman added.
Kartman also denied charges that Washington has been using food aid as a political lever and said "there are no conditions" that the U.S. government has attached to any aid.

Kartman said he could not comment on the status of Cargill Grain Co's recent approval to export two million tonnes of grain to Korea, saying it was a commercial deal and that he did not know the specifics of the financing.
